prompt_text: What is the best service to check if AI engines like ChatGPT recommend my small business?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there’s no single “official” service that tells you whether ChatGPT (or other LLMs) will recommend your business. Best practical approach is a two-part strategy: 1) test LLMs directly (Perplexity, Bing Chat, ChatGPT with browsing/Bard) and 2) use local‑SEO/knowledge‑management tools (Yext, BrightLocal, Moz Local, Whitespark) to make sure AI has accurate, high‑quality data to pull from.

Concrete recommendations

- If you just want to check (quick & free)
  - Query multiple AI engines and ask the same question: e.g. “Recommend Italian restaurants in [city]” or “Do you recommend [Business Name] in [city]?” Try ChatGPT (with browsing or plugins if available), Bing Chat, Perplexity.ai, Google Bard, You.com. Perplexity and Bing are useful because they tend to cite sources.
  - Note whether the model names your business, what sources it cites (if any), and whether the info is correct.

- If you want ongoing coverage and to influence LLM recommendations (paid / business grade)
  - Yext, Synup, or Uberall — they centralize your business “knowledge” (hours, services, menus, FAQs, photos) and distribute it to search engines, maps, directories and some AI platforms. Yext also advertises integrations with LLMs/AI assistants.
  - BrightLocal, Moz Local, Whitespark — focused on local citations, reviews, ranking, and monitoring. Good for reputation and local search signals that LLMs often rely on.
  - SEMrush / Ahrefs — track web presence and backlinks (helps LLMs find credible sources).

What to do to increase the chance an AI will recommend you
- Claim and fully complete Google Business Profile, Apple Maps, Bing Places, Yelp, Facebook.
- Publish structured data (schema.org) on your site: LocalBusiness, FAQPage, Product/Menu, Service. LLMs and search crawlers use this.
- Get reviews on major platforms and respond to them.
- Create clear service pages, FAQ pages, and an “About” page with location, hours and contact.
- Get listed in reputable directories and local news/citation sites (build trust signals).
- Add a knowledge/FAQ page designed for snippet extraction (short Q&A lines).

How to measure success
- Repeat the LLM queries periodically and log which engines mention you and what sources they cite.
- Monitor local rankings and citation accuracy with BrightLocal/Moz.
- If you use Yext or similar, monitor their analytics/dashboard for knowledge sync status.

If you want, I can:
- Run sample queries for your business (give me name + city) across suggested prompts, and report what different AI engines return.
- Recommend the single best paid product for your budget and goals (local SEO vs. enterprise AI distribution) if you tell me your priorities.
session_note: run_channel caveat: API results can differ from logged-in consumer apps, no memory, no personalization.
